findings.claim: Metricool's 2026 Instagram Study of 24,364,803 posts across 375,118 accounts, comparing Jan to Feb 2025 with Jan to Feb 2026, found carousels generate nine times more saves than single-image posts and outperform single images on every major metric.
findings.sourceTitle: Metricool's 2026 Instagram Study Reveals Reels and Carousels Are Reshaping Platform Strategy

findings.claim: In the same Metricool 2026 study, single-image posts fell year over year on every axis: reach down 21.96%, interactions down 25.41%, engagement down 45.98%.
Metricool's 2026 study reports Reels drew more than four times the interactions of single-image posts, and average Reels watch time rose to 8.5 seconds, more than double the prior year.
Metricool's 2026 study found posts that used hashtags averaged 31.70% fewer views and 33.89% fewer interactions than the platform average across the Jan 2025 to Feb 2026 window.
Metricool's 2026 study found posts containing a question drew 36.70% more comments, and posts with an explicit comment-focused call to action drew 202.78% more comments.

Socialinsider's 2026 Instagram benchmark report, 35 million posts across 447,613 active pages for January to December 2025, puts engagement rate by format at carousels 0.50%, Reels 0.48% and single images 0.33%, against an all-format average of 0.45%. The same figures a year earlier were 0.55%, 0.52% and 0.37%.

Socialinsider's 2026 benchmark data shows the median brand posting cadence as roughly 8 Reels, 7 single images and 5 carousels per month, so carousels remain the least-published of the three formats despite leading on engagement rate.

Socialinsider's 2026 saves-per-post data shows carousels and Reels roughly tied and both far ahead of single images at scale: for accounts with 100K to 1M followers, 98 saves per carousel and 96 per Reel versus 43 per image.

Sotrender's August 2026 cross-study review reports Instagram reach is broadly contracting: Metricool measured Reels reach down 35% year over year and overall post reach down 31% across 1,059,949 accounts, while Socialinsider put the average reach rate at 3.50%, down 12% year over year.
findings.sourceTitle: Instagram Reach Is Down in 2026: What the Data Actually Says

findings.claim: Sotrender's August 2026 review cites Buffer's analysis of over 52 million posts showing median Instagram engagement fell from 7.3% in 2024 to 5.4% in 2025, a 26% drop, and notes a growing share of Reels views now comes from non-followers.

Later's 2026 algorithm guide states shares and sends are now a top ranking signal, with Adam Mosseri confirming content people send to friends carries significant weight in wider distribution. It also notes carousels now support up to 20 slides and that Reels up to 3 minutes are eligible for Explore distribution.
findings.sourceTitle: Instagram algorithm in 2026: rank signals for growth

findings.claim: In a July 2026 Q&A, Adam Mosseri said hashtags work but have never been a good way to increase reach, helping only slightly on the margins. The recommended practice is a handful of precise tags describing the subject rather than thirty generic ones, with real distribution coming from recommendations in the first day or two after posting.
findings.sourceTitle: Do hashtags still work on Instagram in 2026? Mosseri finally settled it

findings.claim: Dash Social's 2026 Home Goods benchmark of 3,363 Instagram handles for July 1 to December 31, 2025 reports average video views of 104K per post and Instagram views up 45%, concluding Reels remain the strongest format for discovery in the home and interiors category.
findings.sourceTitle: 2026 Home Goods Industry Benchmarks, Dash Social

findings.claim: For the adjacent real estate category, Apaya's 2026 benchmark roundup cites Dash Social's 0.3% Instagram engagement rate for July to December 2024 alongside a suggested cadence of 3 Reels plus 4 carousel or image posts per week, while warning the sample size is undisclosed and that Hootsuite's differently calculated figure for the same sector is 3.70%, a twelvefold gap.
findings.sourceTitle: Real Estate Social Media Benchmarks 2026: Engagement Rates by Platform
